author: Chuck Ballaro
title: WRESTLING: Tarpons, Mantas cruise to district dual wins - NewsBreak
text:
By Chuck Ballaro ,
16 hours ago
PUNTA GORDA – For years, wrestling coaches wanted the FHSAA to install a state dual format to bring a more team-oriented facet to the sport.
Unfortunately, not every program can plug in 14 wrestlers to compete in every weight class. Many schools have decided to not even take part if they’re going to fall behind by forfeits.
At the District 2A-11 wrestling duals Wednesday at the Wally Keller Gymnasium, only three teams took part. Of them, the top two who were expected to battle for the championship did just that.
Host Charlotte overcame a slow start to blow the doors off Riverdale for the district title with a 57-7 victory.
Meanwhile at Lemon Bay, the Mantas played host to two teams, as well, with similar results. Lemon Bay rolled Sarasota Military and Lakewood en route to the District 1A-11 title.
Charlotte will host the regional duals next Thursday, with Riverdale joining them. They will also be joined by coach Evan Robinson, who had to sit this one out.
Assistant coach Rob Hoff, filling in for Robinson, said he thought the Raiders would give them a better battle than they did.
“We scored the match in our heads and felt it would be tight. If our kids didn’t wrestle well, we could be in trouble. But we came out and the kids were on fire. They pulled out the points and the shots and it worked out,” Hoff said.
Riverdale won two of the first four matches to take an early 7-6 lead. Eric Bush took a major decision at 120 and Logan Miller won 7-2 at 138.
The Raiders never had their hands raised in victory again as Charlotte ran the table with 10 straight wins, six by pin and another by forfeit. Jake Austin started the run with a pin at 144. After Kenneth Torres squeaked out an 8-7 decision at 150, Zak Wendt, Michael Hernandez, Jett Newell and Nate Cortes cradled their opponents to put the match out of reach.
With just three teams, they played round robin. Both Charlotte and Riverdale took care of outmatched Fort Myers. The Tarpons moved several wrestlers up a weight class as they beat the Green Wave 71-9 while Riverdale took them handily 60-11 to set up the championship match.
Riverdale coach Keith Evans said even though things started well with Bush and Miller doing what they needed, it’s tough to keep it up 14 strong against a program like Charlotte.
“The Tarpons are tough all the way through. In a dual it takes a whole team effort and there isn’t a weak spot for those guys,” Evans said. “In the close matches, we have to do better there.”
Evans lamented that there weren’t more teams participating. A fourth team that was supposed to compete backed out at the last minute.
“It’s sad, especially when you have an 11- or 12-team district like us and only three show up,” Evans said. “You can only control what you can control.”
Hoff said the Tarpons looks great as they head for regionals.
“We’re looking pretty good. We have a few tweaks to make and some kids battling injury and illness. If we can get healthy, we can be in there with everybody,” Hoff said.
DISTRICT 1A-11
Meanwhile in Englewood, the same round-robin format was employed when Booker scratched. That left the Mantas to boat race Sarasota Military 76-4 and Lakewood, 73-6.
Lemon Bay boasts nine wrestlers in the latest Kabra Top 25 rankings and filled out its matches on Wednesday by using Addison Silk from the girls' team to fill out the roster. She recorded a pair of forfeit victories.
"Everybody banded together," Lemon Bay coach Jeff Ragan said. "We've got a couple of kids that got the crud and aren't feeling well, so we had a few that couldn't wrestle today.
"We shifted guys around, we bumped guys up, we filled holes and had one of our girls weigh in just so we could bump around."
Silk's inclusion at 106 allowed Talon Truisi move up to 113 and take care of business at that weight. Lemon Bay's other ranked wrestlers – Logan Dean (120), James Bauer (126), Tristan Nee (138), Justus Hatch (144), Elliott Sear (150 and 157), Jason Perez-Mesa (157 and 165), Evan Saunoris (175) and Atticus Randall (195) – all cruised, some while experimenting. Saunoris moved up from 165 to win his two matches.
Lemon Bay's lone defeats came at 215 against Lakewood and 285 against Sarasota Military.
Ragan said the most frustrating aspect of Wednesday's duals was small field, which was unexpected following a raucous preseason debate over the dual meet's date.
"A lot of them argued and fussed to make it January when we used to do it in December and then all the teams that argued didn't come," Ragan said.
In the end, though, Wednesday's duals were just another opportunity for Lemon Bay to continue building the program. Mixed in during a busy couple of weeks will be the Region 1A-3 dual meet on Thursday at Lemon Bay.
"We're building a program. That was our goal when I got here," Ragan said. "I wanted to build back what my father had built so many years ago and build that enthusiasm and excitement. So hopefully we'll pack in the crowd next Thursday for regions, where that's going to matter."
– Sports editor Patrick Obley contributed to this report
